messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I’m seeing a steady increase in page-eviction counters on pool5/card8 over the last 24h. Not a big spike but linear growth. Could be early page retirement.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-monitor pool5/card8 page_evictions=124 -> 198 (24h) | ECC_CORR=8 -> 12 | xid_errors=2 | action_required=review
Maria: thanks. can you paste the perf counters and kernel logs? want to see if ECC correctable errors correlate with evictions.
Alex: quick dump below (last 100 lines):\n```\nGPU: pool5/card8\npage_evictions: 198\necc_correctable: 12\necc_uncorrectable: 0\nxid_errors: 2 (Xid 13 transient)\nPCIe_link_retrain: 0\nlast_remap_ts: 1795120000\n```\nPriya: Xid 13 usually indicates a GPU kernel fault but transient ones can be noise. the steady page_evictions + rising ECC_CORR suggests memory cells are getting unreliable. Recommend draining for write-heavy workloads and running memtest.
Jordan: if we drain card8 that reduces capacity in us-west1 pool5 by ~10%. we have two big reserved jobs tonight. ops impact could be visible. can we shift jobs to pool6? pool6 has free slots but higher latency.
Alex: I tried a live remap probe: `nvml-tool remap-probe --gpu=card8 --rows=0-64` -> returned 3 remapped rows, no reboot required. probe failed to fully stabilize (remap count increased afterwards).
Maria: curious if this is a row remap vs page migration difference. logs from driver: \n```\n[drm:gpu_mem_page_fault] INFO: remap_rows=3, page_migrate_attempts=1, page_migrate_success=0\n```\nPriya: that page_migrate_success=0 is concerning. suggests hardware remap is happening but software migration failing. maybe kernel version mismatch with nvml.
SRE-Lead: propose we do a phased approach: 1) schedule a maintenance window for pool5/card8 tomorrow 02:00 UTC, 2) drain non-critical workloads now, 3) run full memtest + stress, 4) if remap rows continue increasing >300 in 48h, enqueue replacement. agree? :thinking_face:
Jordan: agree with phased approach. I'll shift tonight's reserved jobs to pool6 with a performance lane tag to reduce latency regressions.
Alex: AWS metrics show no host-level hardware alerts. this seems localized to the GPU card. I'll kick off memtest and attach logs here when done.
ops-bot: ACTION: drain initiated for pool5/card8 (non-critical jobs). current evictions=202. drained 6 containers.
Maria: also add a short-term fallback policy in routing to avoid sending large batch calls to pool5/card8. add override in routing config: `route.pool5.card8.max_batch=1`.
Priya: noted. after memtest, run `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and upload to the artifacts bucket.
Alex: memtest kicked off. ETA ~55m. will post results.
SRE-Lead: also consider ordering spare card if this is a trend across other cards. we should check pool5-card* for similar linear trends and correlate by host age.
Maria: good point. can someone run a quick grep across fleet: `fleet-metrics query \"page_evictions>100\" --since=48h --group-by=card`?
Jordan: running now — preliminary: pool5/card7=85, card8=202, card12=140, pool9/card3=95. card8 and card12 look like primary concerns.
Alex: memtest finished: found ECC CORR spikes during pattern tests on bank 3. attaching excerpt: \n```\nmemtest: bank3: correctable_errors=23\nmemtest: total_mem_errors=23\nmemtest: no uncorrectable detected\n```\nPriya: that matches.
SRE-Lead: outcome: replace card8 if remap rows continue to increase after one maintenance cycle. for now keep drained, set routing override, schedule replacement order if card12 shows same in 24h. thanks everyone.
Maria: adding incident note and ticket to hardware queue. ticket #HW-4582.
Alex: will follow up with the replacement ETA and update the ticket.
ops-bot: NOTE: maintenance window scheduled for pool5/card8 at 1795286400 (tomorrow 02:00 UTC).
